evals.prompt: While debugging this issue I wrote a throwaway script and dumped a few JSON files all over the place to inspect them. Where should these files go?
evals.expected_output: Should trigger artifact-hygiene. The result should classify the throwaway script and JSON dumps as disposable run artifacts, place them in mktemp -d / $TMPDIR / /tmp, and delete the temporary artifacts inside the project before finishing, unless the user asks to keep them.

evals.prompt: I just ran a round of Playwright debugging and it left behind a trace, a video, and a few screenshots. Should I commit them to the repo?
evals.expected_output: Should trigger artifact-hygiene. The result should classify the one-off trace/video/screenshots as disposable, never place them in committed paths such as the repo root, docs/, scripts/, or tests/fixtures/, and instead put them in a temporary directory.

evals.prompt: Our CI already uses playwright-report and test-results. Where should these outputs go?
evals.expected_output: Should trigger artifact-hygiene. The result should identify them as workflow-consumed artifacts (already depended on by the repo's workflow), place them in the project's existing gitignored output paths, and not treat them as disposable to be deleted or create a new directory for them.

evals.prompt: I want to create a debug-output/ directory in the repo for these debug artifacts and add a line to .gitignore so I have a place to put them in the future. Is that okay?
evals.expected_output: Should trigger artifact-hygiene. The result should refuse per the hard boundary: do not create or widen .gitignore, config conventions, or repo directories to host disposable artifacts; these are clearly disposable debug artifacts, so place them in a temporary directory.

evals.prompt: Help me fix a logic bug in this login-state check. I'm not asking to generate any files.
evals.expected_output: Should NOT trigger artifact-hygiene; this is a code logic fix and does not involve placing or cleaning up generated files, debug artifacts, or downloads.

evals.prompt: Help me check whether the naming and comments in this code are up to standard.
evals.expected_output: Should NOT trigger artifact-hygiene; this is a code style and contract review, not deciding where generated/debug artifacts should go.

evals.prompt: We generate a weekly coverage report the team now wants to keep in a standard, gitignored reports path going forward. Set up that convention.
evals.expected_output: Should trigger artifact-hygiene. Because the user explicitly asks for a reusable convention, this is the sanctioned exception to the hard boundary: treat the recurring report as a workflow-consumed artifact, place it in a gitignored maintained output path rather than a temporary directory, do not delete it on completion, and keep the convention minimal instead of widening unrelated .gitignore entries or directories.

evals.prompt: Make me a slide deck (an HTML PPT) about our team's AI-First rollout that I can share with the team.
evals.expected_output: Should trigger artifact-hygiene. Because the user explicitly asked for the deck as the end product, classify it as a requested deliverable — not a disposable HTML dump, despite the .html format. Place it in the durable maintained location where similar shared/deliverable docs already live (or ask the user where it belongs if there is no clear peer), do not put it in a temporary/scratchpad directory, and do not delete it on completion.

evals.prompt: Write up the database migration plan as a Markdown doc — I want to keep it in the repo and hand it to the team.
evals.expected_output: Should trigger artifact-hygiene. The user asked for the write-up as the end product to keep. Either SKILL-supported label is acceptable — a requested deliverable or a durable-doc project asset — because both resolve to the same placement; what matters is that it is NOT treated as a disposable investigation note. Place it in the maintained docs path where the team's other kept docs live (or ask if there is no clear peer), and do not delete it on completion. Demonstrates the keep-and-place outcome generalizes beyond decks to prose documents.

evals.prompt: Export the quarterly usage query results to a JSON file I need to send to finance.
evals.expected_output: Should trigger artifact-hygiene. Even though the file is JSON, it is a requested deliverable because the user asked for it as the output they need — it must NOT be classified as a disposable JSON dump by format. Place it in a durable location the user can retrieve it from (or ask where it belongs), do not put it in a temporary/scratchpad directory, and do not delete it on completion. This is the mirror image of a JSON file dumped incidentally during debugging (which is disposable): same format, opposite classification, decided solely by whether the user asked for it as the deliverable.

evals.prompt: During this task I produced a config-looking JSON file, and I honestly can't tell whether it's throwaway scratch or something we'll want to keep. Where should it go?
evals.expected_output: Should trigger artifact-hygiene. This is the genuinely-ambiguous case rule 5 governs: the agent cannot tell whether the artifact is disposable or worth keeping. It should ask the user rather than silently guessing; and if it cannot ask (a non-interactive or CI run), fall back to treating it as disposable in a temporary directory — never silently commit an ambiguous artifact into the repo.

evals.prompt: Before I edit these three config files, should I save a .bak copy of each one, plus a timestamped backup folder, just in case?
evals.expected_output: Should trigger artifact-hygiene. The result should refuse per the hard boundary: do not create .bak / backup / timestamped duplicate copies before editing, because version control already preserves the prior state and such copies are disposable clutter. It should note the only sanctioned exception is a real product feature that must snapshot data (e.g. a pre-upgrade config backup), which should be opt-in and default-off rather than always producing copies.

evals.prompt: I wrote a small setup script that provisions the fail-close routing on this box; it worked. It's the kind of thing I'll need again when I set up the next machine. Where should it live?
evals.expected_output: Should trigger artifact-hygiene. By the reuse test, an automation/bootstrap script a future run or a fresh machine will need again is a project asset, not a disposable run artifact — persist it into the maintained project path rather than leaving it in a temporary directory. Contrast with a one-off script that only serves the current run, which stays disposable in /tmp.
